However, CSF tau and Ptau-181 showed slight increases in treated arms vs slight decreases in placebo, which is not the expected downstream effect if amyloid reduction were translating to neuroprotection. The cognitive endpoint clearly failed. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses were reported. The population was MCI/mild AD, which is a relatively early stage — potentially appropriate for the mechanism but the trial was too short and too small to detect cognitive benefit. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was terminated early due to hepatotoxicity signals (abnormal liver biochemical tests). This is the primary reason the trial failed to complete its pre-specified endpoints. The hepatotoxicity prevented adequate duration of dosing and prevented collection of 26-week CSF data. This is a dose-limiting toxicity / safety termination scenario. The cognitive endpoint also failed in the arms that did complete 26 weeks (15 mg and 35 mg), suggesting that even if the trial had continued, cognitive benefit was not emerging. Multiple failure factors are present: (a) dose-limiting toxicity leading to early termination, (b) wrong timeframe for cognitive endpoints, (c) possible biology-moved-endpoint-flat for the cognitive readout (Aβ reduced but cognition didn't improve), and (d) the trial was underpowered for cognitive endpoints.

Despite robust dose-dependent reductions in CSF and plasma Aβ (up to -60.7% CSF Aβ1-42 at 70 mg), the NTB Z-score cognitive endpoint showed no benefit at 26 weeks in the 15 mg (-0.039) and 35 mg (-0.161) arms. The biology (amyloid reduction) clearly moved but the clinical cognitive endpoint did not improve.

26 weeks is likely insufficient to detect cognitive benefit in MCI/mild AD even with substantial Aβ reduction. The amyloid cascade hypothesis predicts that cognitive benefit from Aβ reduction would require longer treatment duration to manifest as measurable cognitive improvement.

Total N=70 across 4 arms (approximately 15-18 per arm) is grossly underpowered to detect cognitive benefit in MCI/mild AD at 26 weeks. The trial was likely designed primarily as a biomarker/PD study rather than a powered cognitive efficacy study.
